written.myAnswer: A caution sign warns people to be alert and take extra care in the area.
Examples of explosive chemicals include picric acid, nitroglycerin and TNT.
Examples of corrosive chemicals include sulfuric acid, hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide.
Keep explosive chemicals away from heat, flames and sparks, avoid shocks or rough handling, and handle and store them carefully according to laboratory instructions.
Asphyxiant chemicals, including chemicals that release suffocating gases or displace oxygen, can cause suffocation.
Signs and symbols warn people of hazards and indicate the precautions needed to handle them safely.
A trefoil symbol identifies a radiation hazard; an asphyxiation warning identifies a risk of suffocation.
Warning signs and symbols identify hazards, alert people to danger, and indicate precautions to help prevent laboratory accidents.
Explosive chemicals may explode, causing injury and damage. Toxic chemicals can poison people and animals, sometimes causing serious illness or death.

Prevent such accidents by inspecting and maintaining tankers and containers, using safe handling and transport procedures, training staff, displaying toxic-gas warnings, and promptly alerting nearby people and emergency services if a leak occurs.
